evidence: nameserver-serves-the-vpn-network: network_vpn.pp:31-32 passes allowed_networks ["198.51.100.0/24"] (params openvpn_network 198.51.100.0); the baseline template named.conf.options.erb:3 renders listen-on { 127.0.0.1; 198.51.100.0/24; } so bind binds the bridge address 198.51.100.1:53, and :9 renders allow-query { localhost;  198.51.100.0/24;  }, exactly what the ss count and the allow-query regex expect

the-client-resolves-and-reaches-the-wan-through-the-server: network_vpn.pp:41-44 composes firewall_addon_openvpn_server with wan_iface p8test0 (params) and bridge br0; its :17-21 (202 br0->wan accept, 203 replies, 205 MASQUERADE out the wan) is what lets a tunnel client's TCP connection reach 203.0.113.1 behind p8test0 with source 203.0.113.50 (the server's p8test0 address), with the stand-in drops appended after the class's rules so only those rules can pass it; :1-4 (internal caching nameserver for the VPN) supports the recursive NOERROR answer from 198.51.100.1; the action only adds a client-side host route (redirect-gateway filtered, declared), the effect is dig + the WAN server's own view, not the action's output

forwarding-and-nat-to-the-wan: firewall_addon_openvpn_server.pp:21 declares nat POSTROUTING outiface $wan_iface proto all jump MASQUERADE -> '-A POSTROUTING -o p8test0 -j MASQUERADE'; :17-19 give the three FORWARD lines expected (br0->p8test0 accept, p8test0->br0 with state RELATED,ESTABLISHED, br0->br0) and :25 sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward 1; network_vpn.pp:42-43 passes wan_iface p8test0 / bridge br0 under the params fixture

whole file: all 11 checks are negative controls (no invariants); the 7 mutating checks declare every change (p8vpnuser account, the lab IPv6/-4 named fixture, the WAN-side TCP server and the 3 stand-in drops, the peer's openvpn client/routes, the second CBC-only client) and judge on read-only effects; no probe reaches a host other than the node and the declared peer; no mismatch control is required by the validator; the cipher check's effect is the negotiated Data Channel cipher, not a self-supplied verdict, and the password-rejection control lives in openvpn_server's set (wrong-password-rejected)

purpose covered: Purpose (VPN gateway: OpenVPN server with user auth whose clients resolve via the VPN's own caching nameserver on the bridge and reach the WAN through the server) matches network_vpn.pp:1-4 and the four composed classes at :29-60. Tested end to end with a real client on the peer: PAM-account login and pool address on 198.51.100.0/24 with the pushed DNS 198.51.100.1, the VPN nameserver answering through the tunnel over a stand-in default drop (1301 counted), a recursive NOERROR for a real name, a WAN-side TCP connection seen from 203.0.113.50 (202/203/205 counted), and a client on the class's own cipher AES-256-CBC (:25, :57) negotiating it. Left out, honestly listed: client isolation, bridge/server at boot, the hairpin rule 204's behaviour, the data channel's compression (an openvpn_server finding) and the composed classes' own behaviours, all exercised in those classes' own sets; parameter variants (one params fixture). The lab named runs with -4 (declared environment fixture: the NAT lab has no IPv6), so recursion under an IPv6-routed host is not shown; the set states that as an HQ question.
